purpose: Paired Native-vs-MAF evaluation of Durable Verified Success on the frozen 29-task suite

NATIVE.description: The coding agent running in its ordinary execution mode with no MAF orchestration or intervention. Its own execution artifact is still graded by the same independent, controller-side verification pipeline used for MAF.

MAF.description: The same coding agent running under the MAF adaptive mode controller (src/domain/mode-controller.ts) with control/assurance behavior enabled: adaptive STRICT/GUIDED/SOLO_NATIVE mode transitions driven by runtime signals, and controller-side independent verification after execution.

treatmentPolicy.note: Frozen policy dimensions for Protocol v1. Runtime mode transitions the controller makes within this policy are adaptive by design (see EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md section 6); the POLICY governing those transitions is what is frozen here, not any single run's transitions.
treatmentPolicy.interventionPolicy: AdaptiveModeController default policy (src/domain/mode-controller.ts), unmodified for this protocol
treatmentPolicy.retryPolicy: Executor-reported retryCount only; no additional MAF-imposed retry ceiling beyond the adaptive controller's own mode-driven behavior
treatmentPolicy.verificationPolicy: Controller-side CuratorIndependentVerifier (src/evaluation/curator-verifier.ts): hidden grader + SMOKE regression, run after participant execution, never observed by the participant
treatmentPolicy.escalation: STRICT -> GUIDED -> SOLO_NATIVE per AdaptiveModeController transition rules; no manual escalation for this protocol
treatmentPolicy.recoveryBehavior: src/domain/recovery.ts classifyFailure-driven provider-transient handling only; no additional MAF-side recovery beyond what the adapter itself reports
treatmentPolicy.modelRouting: NONE — same frontier model and effort as NATIVE for every paired run
treatmentPolicy.sandboxing: Same controller-owned, per-run temporary workspace and execution environment as NATIVE
treatmentPolicy.costControls: src/domain/budget.ts HARD allocation mode at the frozen per-run budget ceiling below; no separate MAF-only budget

modelConfiguration.note: Same model/version/effort used for both NATIVE and MAF_ADAPTIVE arms of every paired run. Resolved per the mission header (MODEL: Claude Sonnet 5, Effort: High).

runCountRationale: 29 tasks x 2 arms x 3 repetitions = 174 participant runs. See EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md section 15 for the N=1/3/5 cost-and-runtime scenario table and rationale; N=3 matches the repetition count protocol.json already uses for local ABI stress validation (execution.repetitions) and is the minimum that lets task-level aggregation (majority-of-3) reduce single-run stochasticity before pairing.
timeoutRationale: 30 minutes per participant run. Distinct from the local ABI grader timeout (evaluation/protocol.json execution.timeoutMs = 120000, which bounds fast deterministic fixture checks, not frontier agent execution) and from the independent verifier's own grader/regression timeouts (src/evaluation/curator-verifier.ts DEFAULT_GRADER_TIMEOUT_MS=30000, DEFAULT_REGRESSION_TIMEOUT_MS=20000), which run after participant timing has already stopped.

budget.note: Enforced via src/domain/budget.ts computeAllocation/authorizeSpend HARD mode, identically for both arms. See EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md section 9 for the derivation and the N=1/3/5 total-experiment cost scenarios computed from Claude Sonnet 5 published per-token pricing.

randomization.method: xmur3-seeded mulberry32 Fisher-Yates shuffle of the frozen 29 task IDs; arm order derived from shuffled-position parity (even index = NATIVE_FIRST, odd index = MAF_FIRST)

invalidRunPolicy.definition: evaluation/protocol.json invalidRuns semantics, unmodified: invalid runs never count as DVS and are reported separately from the valid-run denominator
invalidRunPolicy.modelArmFailure: An arm failure the participant itself caused (task not attempted correctly, candidate produced but grader FAILs, participant crashes on its own logic) is a valid run with a non-DVS outcome; it is never rerun
invalidRunPolicy.infrastructureFailure: executionStatus in {INFRA_FAILURE, TIMEOUT, CANCELLED, QUOTA_EXHAUSTED} or a providerError/infrastructureError present, per src/evaluation/types.ts isInfrastructureFailure
invalidRunPolicy.rerunPermitted: Only for runs classified as EXPERIMENT_INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE (provider outage, quota exhaustion, tool/workspace/runner crash unrelated to either arm's own behavior); never for an ordinary arm failure

stoppingRule.description: Run the fixed N=3 repetitions for every one of the 29 tasks x 2 arms; do not stop early because an aggregate trend appears in either direction
exceptions: safety or integrity failure (leakage, nondeterminism, private-material exposure) — stop the affected task or the whole run per EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md section 20
provider outage exceeding a reasonable retry window

contaminationRule: After scoring begins, the benchmark suite, graders, MAF policy, Native configuration, model/version, effort, timeout, task prompts, run count, and statistical plan are frozen. A material defect found mid-run stops the affected experiment and is recorded as an incident rather than silently patched; a benchmark defect produces a suite v2, a protocol defect produces a protocol v2.

dryRun.taskSource: evaluation/experiments/dry-run (synthetic, not part of the frozen 29-task suite)
